result.markdown: --- title: "[vals.fmt_fraction()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Format values as mixed fractions. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-tables/blob/main/great_tables/_formats_vals.py#L1181-L1255){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python vals.fmt_fraction( x, accuracy="low", simplify=True, layout="inline", use_seps=True, pattern="{x}", sep_mark=",", locale=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} With numeric values we can perform mixed-fraction-based formatting. The `accuracy` parameter controls the type of fractions generated: use a keyword (`"low"`, `"med"`, `"high"`) to get denominators of up to 1, 2, or 3 digits, or supply a positive integer to fix the denominator (e.g., `2` for halves, `4` for quarters). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [X]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of values to be formatted. [accuracy]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["low"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The accuracy of the fraction. Use `"low"` for denominators up to 1 digit (e.g., halves, thirds, quarters, etc.), `"med"` for up to 2-digit denominators, `"high"` for up to 3-digit denominators, or a positive integer for a fixed denominator. The default is `"low"`. [simplify]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : When `accuracy` is an integer, should the fraction be simplified via GCD reduction? For example, with `accuracy=4` and a value of `0.5`, `simplify=True` yields `"1/2"` while `simplify=False` yields `"2/4"`. The default is `True`. [layout]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["inline"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"inline"` for baseline fractions with a standard slash (e.g., `3/4`), `"diagonal"` for raised/lowered numerals with a fraction slash character (HTML only). The default is `"inline"`. [use_seps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use digit grouping separators in the whole-number part. The default is `True`. [pattern]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["{x}"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A formatting pattern that allows for decoration of the formatted value. The formatted value is represented by the `{x}` and all other characters are interpreted as string literals. [sep_mark]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[","]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The mark to use as a thousands separator. The default is `","`. [locale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An optional locale ID that can be used for applying a locale-specific thousands separator. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of formatted values is returned. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#e4fef475 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from great_tables import vals vals.fmt_fraction([1.5, 0.25, 3.75]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['1 1/2', '1/4', '3 3/4'] ``` ::: :::
